name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real data on its impact without risking disruption. The trade-off is delayed immediate gains, but we avoid breaking builds or annoying devs with bad suggestions. After the week, we’ll measure accuracy and noise, then decide whether to roll it out fully or tweak.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode normalizes noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments, including the useful ones, because PR-Agent’s output is already treated as background static. Instead, run it on a controlled subset of PRs (e.g., low-risk changes or new contributors) to measure signal vs. noise without poisoning the entire review culture. Settle the argument by tracking whether reviewers act on PR-Agent suggestions *after* the test period—if the hit rate doesn’t improve, the tool’s value is zero.
